```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import Markdown

root = Path("..") if Path("../data").exists() else Path(".")
df = pd.read_csv(root / "data/processed/compensation_all_years.csv")
chg = pd.read_csv(root / "data/processed/matched_changes.csv")
years = sorted(df["year"].unique())
first, last = years[0], years[-1]

med = df.groupby("year")["midpoint"].median()
top = df.assign(t=df["midpoint"] >= 150000).groupby("year")["t"].mean() * 100
roles = df.groupby("year").size()
last_pair = chg[chg["to_year"] == last]
big = (last_pair["max_rate_change_pct"] > 10).mean() * 100
typical = last_pair["max_rate_change_pct"].median()

Markdown(f"""
**The short version.** The median pay-range midpoint rose from ${med[first]/1000:,.0f}k in {first} to ${med[last]/1000:,.0f}k in {last}, up {(med[last]/med[first]-1)*100:.1f}%.
Roles with a midpoint of $150k or more went from {top[first]:.1f}% to {top[last]:.1f}% of the list.
For roles on both the {last_pair['from_year'].iloc[0]} and {last} lists, the median change in the maximum rate was {typical:.1f}%, and {big:.0f}% of them rose more than 10%.
The list covers {roles[last]:,} position titles in {last} ({roles[first]:,} in {first}).
""")
```

```{python}
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-height: 2.6
fig, (a, b) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7.2, 2.6))
a.plot(med.index.astype(str), med.values / 1000, marker="o", color="#2A78D6", lw=2)
a.set_title("Median range midpoint ($k)", fontsize=9, loc="left")
b.bar(top.index.astype(str), top.values, color="#2A78D6", width=0.5)
b.set_title("Roles at $150k or more (%)", fontsize=9, loc="left")
for ax in (a, b):
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=8)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

**How to read this.** Each row in the list is a position title with a minimum and maximum annual base rate, not a person's salary. The City says its 2026 list reflects a new salary structure for exempt (non-union) roles, so 2026 changes mix pay increases with restructuring. Calgary Police Service, seasonal and on-call roles are not included. Overtime and benefits are not in the rates.

*Source: City of Calgary Open Data, Compensation Disclosure Lists. Full report and interactive charts are on the project site.*
